summary.headline: MPi H1 FY27 revenue rose 40.3% to INR 849.4 crore and PAT 45.4% to INR 158.6 crore, while Q2 operational EBITDA margin fell to 30.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33.6% to INR 430.4 crore in Q2 FY27 and 40.3% to INR 849.4 crore in H1. Emerging businesses grew 92% in H1 and reached 34.5% of revenue, while core business grew 23%. Operational EBITDA rose 17.5% in Q2 to INR 131.3 crore, with margin at 30.5%, held back by forex, input costs and freight. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% and a 25% CAGR for FY27-29.

segments.name: Core business (domestic cards, Government ID, digital banking and automation, bundled fulfilment)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 294 crore in Q2 (+23% from INR 239 crore) and INR 556 crore in H1 (+23%). Growth driven by higher domestic card volumes, a new debit card logistics mandate from a large PSU bank, and transit card projects.

segments.name: Emerging business (international cards, metal cards, tax stamps, RFID)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 136 crore in Q2 (+63% from INR 84 crore) and INR 293 crore in H1 (+92%). Share of revenue was 31.7% in Q2 versus 25.9% a year ago. Metal cards and tax stamps are described as margin-accretive.

segments.name: International operations (Nigeria, UK, other regions)
segments.commentary: Nigeria bureau started in Q1 and added more than 10 customers in Q2 (over 20 in H1 per management). UK personalisation bureau is now operational, with revenue expected in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% reiterated; management says it is on course.
FY27-FY29 revenue CAGR of about 25% indicated.
H2 expected to be stronger, consistent with history; historical H1/H2 revenue split of 45-55% to 55-45%, which may shift with new geographies.
UK bureau expected to contribute revenue from H2 FY27; one more large developed market to be set up by end of FY27.
Margin improvement expected as metal cards, tax stamps and export mix grow, subject to forex and geopolitical conditions; management says margins should be judged on an annualised basis.
Seeding costs for new businesses and geographies were INR 16.5 crore after tax in H1 and are expected to support margins as they earn.
capex_capacity: Utilisation: plastic card capacity about 80%, metal cards 55-60%, tax stamps 70-75%.
Around INR 240 crore earmarked from IPO proceeds for capex over the next 2-3 years; capacity is not seen as a constraint.
Capex of about INR 135 crore in FY26 and about INR 58 crore in H1 FY27; incremental assets are leased on five-year tenures with depreciation over five years.
Asset life of machines is 7, 10 and 15 years depending on type.
Metal card capacity expansion is progressing as planned.
demand_pricing: Over 30 new customers added in H1 FY27, mostly outside India; more than 10 added in Nigeria in Q2.
Metal card demand is rising in India and internationally; management cites patented manufacturing technology and US metal card market of 30-40 million cards.
Global PVC card issuance is growing 2-4% YoY and metal cards about 15% annualised, per management.
Pricing: PSU contracts are multi-year (2-3 years, sometimes 5) with fixed pricing and force majeure renegotiation clauses; private, cooperative and fintech contracts can be renegotiated.
Raw materials are 75-80% imported (Europe, Singapore, China); input cost rise reflects both rupee depreciation and crude movement.
Top 10 customers contributed just over 52% of H1 FY27 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin rise sequentially while emerging revenue fell QoQ, and what is the H2 pipeline for exports and metal cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin movement to sales and product mix, with a quarter-on-quarter variation expected. It said order timing varies by quarter, and that it is confident of the international guidance for H2. It did not quantify metal card or tax stamp mix.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material import costs passed through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: PSU contracts are fixed for 2-3 years (sometimes 5) with force majeure renegotiation. Private banks, cooperative banks and fintechs can be renegotiated. Management said pricing factors in variances.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight cost roughly double YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight is a direct cost tied to the integrated logistics business, which delivers cards end-to-end to customer beneficiaries. It rises with bundled service volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has depreciation risen sharply, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose to INR 22.4 crore in Q2 from INR 11.9 crore due to leased assets on five-year tenures. Management expects it to normalise as INR 240 crore of IPO-funded capex comes in.

qa_highlights.question: What are the UK and US opportunities and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: The UK business is with the largest new UK bank and revenue is expected in H2. US sales teams are in place and some revenue is hoped for this year. Management would not name large bank breakthroughs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation and how will international expansion be supported?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastic card capacity is about 80%, metal 55-60%, and tax stamps 70-75%. Capacity is not seen as a constraint given the INR 240 crore capex plan.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from forex (rupee depreciation), crude-linked and freight input costs; Q2 EBITDA growth (17.5%) lagged revenue growth (33.6%).
Working capital days rose to 96 from 74 a year ago; receivable days are seasonally high in H1.
Lumpy quarterly revenue from large program rollouts and new customer onboarding; management asks to judge on a YTD basis.
Top 10 customers contribute about 52% of revenue, concentration risk.
Depreciation step-up from leased assets; watch whether it normalises as IPO-funded capex is deployed.
UK revenue ramp in H2 and any large UK or US bank wins; the US timeline is still uncertain.
Geopolitical tensions and forex remain outside management control.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and the international push, but cautious and non-committal on margins, forex and quarter-to-quarter revenue timing. Management deflected on specific customer names and on competitor depreciation comparisons.
key_quotes: Given the nature of our business, the onboarding of new customers and the rollout of large programs can shift revenue between quarters.
We therefore believe our performance is best evaluated on a year-to-date basis, as it gives a more meaningful picture of our underlying growth.
But on an annualized basis, so what we suggest is that the margin have to be looked at an annualized basis.
We will inform as and when we progress.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% (midpoint 32.5%) and guided ~25% CAGR for FY27-29, backed by H1 revenue up 40.3%, 30+ new customers, a UK bureau going live, Nigeria bureau ramp and ~INR 240 crore of IPO-funded capex over 2-3 years, though no specific order values or capacity additions with numbers were given for the guidance.
